task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup role coverage (>=1 Primary Organizer, Shaper, Terminal Scorer on court)
structural roles defined by usage x residual structural influence
separability from talent and role-player counts
methodological_questions: Does coverage (all three roles present) vary across lineups within a team-season, beyond what the roster's role counts force?
Is coverage separable from talent and from raw counts of role-holders or usage?
Does the talent control behave (stable estimates, no sign flips, no collinearity artifacts)?
Are role labels reliable and free of outcome leakage when applied to lineups?
Is there enough lineup exposure per team-season?

historical_evidence.finding: Residual structural influence is not reducible to usage (cosine R2 about 0.09-0.10, residual share about 0.90-0.91) and split-half stability of the residual is rho about +0.67-0.69 (usage-partial rho about +0.56). [prior work] lists [prior work] / RISK:MEASURE_RELIABILITY.

After controlling for regular-season net-rating talent, the adaptation effect was p=0.275 (n=55 series). [prior work] says this cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality (confounding, small sample).

[prior work]'s status is untestable (its verdict field reads inconclusive). Series-level association with winning was underpowered (n=50, p=0.07) and still confounded by team quality. Game-level n was inflated.
Adding usage, lineup and context variables explained about 0-1.7 pp beyond regression to the mean (RTM about 95% of explained variance). This was an adequately powered null (n=40,963 cells).
Star-vs-lineup suppression cells were reported without placebo or matching (RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE). [prior work] says later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

A calibrated simulation fell from 68.9% win accuracy in validation to 54.8% on holdout, against 64.5% for a lineup +/- baseline. [prior work] flags a construction artifact (C_artifact) and same-pipeline validation.
A feasibility gate passed (movers, decoys, and a non-collinearity check with |rho|<0.90). Mover count and rho differed between the prereg record and the final output.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Separating a team-process effect from talent using a series-level unit.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with [prior work] and [prior work] (n about 55 series).
Recorded as A_unanswerable ([prior work], [prior work]): inflated game-level n; the series level was underpowered and still confounded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Descriptive star-lineup suppression cells without placebo or matching.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE; failure mechanism unclear in [prior work].

failed_approaches.what_failed: Same-pipeline validation of a simulation against team-level baselines.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: a validation-to-holdout collapse.

evidence_establishes: FAM:[prior work] (supported): residual influence, the quantity that separates Shapers from Role Occupants and Terminals, is mostly not explained by usage and is moderately reproducible within player. Role labels are therefore not a pure usage restatement.
Team-quality confounding has repeatedly blocked inference at small team or series n ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
Explanatory power added by lineup variables beyond a regression-to-the-mean baseline was near zero in one powered test ([prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved measured lineup-level coverage of the three roles, or its within-team variance.
Nothing retrieved tested whether coverage is separable from talent or from counts of role-holders.
Nothing retrieved shows how a talent control behaves (stability, sign) in a lineup-level model.
Nothing retrieved shows whether coverage predicts any outcome. The question as posed is a measurement and validity question, not an outcome claim.
own_inferences: Mechanical dependence is likely. Roles are defined by usage median x residual sign, so high-usage lineups are more likely to contain an organizer or terminal, and coverage correlates with the count of role-holders by construction. Separability must therefore be tested against a count-matched null, not just by partial correlation.

Within-team variance in coverage is probably non-trivial given rotations, but is bounded by roster composition. Many team-seasons may have most lineups all-covered or all-uncovered, which would make the variance claim trivially true or too thin to test.
With 90 team-seasons, team-level inference is power-limited, but lineup-level data (hundreds of thousands of possessions) permit within-team estimates if clustered by team-season.
Talent control 'behaving' needs an operational definition: stable sign and magnitude across seasons and specifications, VIF below a threshold, and no reversal when adding or removing counts.
Outcome-derived talent (same-season net rating) would induce leakage, and role labels built from the same games used for evaluation could inflate coverage-outcome links.
uncertainties: How 'talent' is to be measured is not specified. The data have no independent talent rating, so it must be derived from lagged data or a box-score or play-by-play composite.
The exact role-assignment rule (median thresholds, minimum initiations, per season or rolling) is not given. The glossary notes that role labels such as Connector varied between studies.
Role reliability: FAM:[prior work] reports split-half rho about 0.67, so about a third of role label variance may be noise, and labels near thresholds will flip.
The lineup unit (5-man stint vs. possession) and minimum exposure are unspecified.
I did not read the full family records for [prior work] (the result text was cut), so effect-size details beyond the excerpt are unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The evidence moved the decision from a plain proceed toward proceed_with_changes. FAM:[prior work] raises confidence that roles are not a usage restatement and have moderate reliability. [prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] argue for lineup-level units over series-level units, a regression-to-the-mean baseline, and explicit confounding controls, so the design uses those.

blocking_constraints.text: Coverage is partly determined by the count of role-holders and by usage, which are in the role definition. Separability needs a count-preserving permutation null.
Role labels have split-half reliability around 0.67 (FAM:[prior work]); label misclassification attenuates separability estimates.

prior_work.summary: Role definition and moderate reliability (not a usage restatement) are partly established by FAM:[prior work]. Lineup-level coverage variation, separability from talent and counts, and talent-control behaviour have no retrieved prior test.

risks.text: Coverage is a deterministic function of which role-holders are on court; correlation with counts and usage is partly built in.
Role labels are noisy (split-half rho about 0.67); lineups near thresholds flip classification.
Coverage is tied to roster quality, minutes, and opponent or garbage-time context. Talent is hard to measure independently of role.
Roles or talent estimated on the same games used to evaluate lineups would leak information. Use lagged or split-sample estimates.
Role labels derive from structural influence computed from possession outcomes. A talent control from net rating shares this source.
Only 90 team-seasons; many lineups have thin minutes. Lineup-level power does not translate to team-level power.
Most 5-man lineups play few possessions, and uncovered lineups may be rare for some teams.
Several specifications, talent proxies and thresholds could be tried; the primary tests must be fixed in advance.
Role assignments and league style change across the 2022-26 seasons and between regular season and playoffs.

design.estimand: (a) Within-team-season variance of lineup coverage (share of lineup-possessions with at least one Primary Organizer, Shaper and Terminal Scorer on court) versus a null that permutes lineups within the team-season. (b) Partial association between coverage and the role-holder count plus usage sum, and between coverage and talent, estimated with mixed models. (c) Stability of the talent coefficient across specifications.
design.unit: Lineup (5-man stint aggregate) within team-season, with possession-level data aggregated to lineups. Team-season is the cluster. Team-season (n=90) is the unit for any between-team statement.
design.sample: 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (the 2025-26 regular season is complete). Playoffs are analysed separately as a secondary set. Exclude garbage time. Lineups need at least a pre-registered minimum of about 50 possessions. Fix this and the role thresholds before any outcome is looked at.
design.power: Lineup-level power is adequate given 420,993 possessions, but effective n is limited by clustering within 90 team-seasons. Report the number of eligible lineups per team-season and the design effect. Team-level claims are exploratory unless a minimum detectable effect (for example r of about 0.30 at n=90) is stated and met.
design.controls: Assign roles from a prior-season or odd-game split, evaluated on even games, to avoid leakage. Use an independent talent proxy: lagged-season player rating or a minutes-weighted player rating built on separate games from the evaluation games, not same-season net rating. Controls: role-holder count, usage sum, minutes, and opponent strength. Report VIF and fit with and without counts. Use a count-preserving permutation null. Propagate role-label uncertainty by bootstrapping role assignments (split-half).
design.falsification: (1) Within-team permutation: lineups reshuffled across the team's rotation preserving player counts; coverage variance beyond the null is required. (2) Placebo roles: randomly relabel roles preserving the marginal role distribution; the effect must vanish. (3) Talent-control sanity: the coefficient must keep its sign across seasons, split halves, and with or without counts. A sign flip or VIF above 5 counts as failure of 'talent control behaves'. (4) A same-pipeline validation is not accepted; use a held-out season (2025-26) for confirmation.
design.multiplicity: Three primary tests (variation, separability, talent-control stability) at alpha 0.05 with Holm correction. Everything else, including playoffs and talent-proxy variants, is labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if all three hold: (a) observed within-team coverage variance exceeds the permutation null (Holm-adjusted p<0.05) with at least a pre-set share of team-seasons showing meaningful variation; (b) the coverage-talent partial association remains distinguishable from zero after counts and usage, and coverage retains explanatory variation not reproduced by the count-preserving null; (c) talent-coefficient sign and magnitude stable (within a pre-set tolerance) across specifications with VIF below 5. If (a) fails because coverage is near-constant, report as untestable or non-informative. If separability disappears under the count-preserving null, report as artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived play-type graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available 2026-07-13 (2025-26 regular season and playoffs complete); freeze extraction snapshot and classifier version with hash before analysis.
